notes.text: **[Zohar I 48a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Bereshit_78.193)** (Bereshit) — אֲבָל בְּשַׁבָּת סֻכַּת שָׁלוֹם אִתְפְּרִיסָא עַל עָלְמָא... וּבְגִין כָּךְ בִּקְדוּשָּׁא דְיוֹמָא מְבָרְכִינָן הַפּוֹרֵס סֻכַּת שָׁלוֹם עָלֵינוּ וְעַל כָּל עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְעַל יְרוּשָׁלַםִ: "On Shabbat the shelter of peace is spread over the world... therefore in the holiness of the day we bless 'Who spreads the shelter of peace over us, over all His people Israel, and over Jerusalem.'" The Zohar continues (78:194): אַמַּאי עַל יְרוּשָׁלָם, אֶלָּא דָא הִיא מְדוֹרָא דְהַהִיא סֻכָּה — Jerusalem is the dwelling of that shelter. This is the basis for his opening: on Shabbat all Israel merit the holiness of Yerushalayim and the Mikdash. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Shulchan Arukh, Orach Chayim 267:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Shulchan_Arukh,_Orach_Chayim_267.3)** — the Shabbat-eve Hashkiveinu: אוֹמֵר וּפְרוֹס סֻכַּת שָׁלוֹם עָלֵינוּ וְעַל יְרוּשָׁלַיִם עִירֶךָ, בא"י הַפּוֹרֵס סֻכַּת שָׁלוֹם עָלֵינוּ וְעַל עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְעַל יְרוּשָׁלַיִם — "spread over us the shelter of peace and over Jerusalem Your city... Who spreads the shelter of peace over us, over His people Israel and over Jerusalem." The liturgy itself joins the Shabbat shelter to Jerusalem. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Bereshit Rabbah 69:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah_69.7)** — דָּבָר אַחֵר מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהֶרְאָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיַעֲקֹב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ בָּנוּי וְחָרֵב וּבָנוּי... מַה נּוֹרָא הַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה זֶה בָּנוּי... וְאֵין זֶה הֲרֵי חָרֵב כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמַר עַל זֶה הָיָה דָוֶה לִבֵּנוּ... כִּי אִם בֵּית אֱלֹהִים בָּנוּי וּמְשֻׁכְלָל לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמַר כִּי חִזַּק בְּרִיחֵי שְׁעָרָיִךְ. "He showed Yaakov the Temple built, destroyed and built again." The Sefaria text attaches 'built and perfected' to 'the house of God'; in paragraph 3 the author rejects that reading and attaches it to 'this is the gate of heaven', with the Matnos Kehunah and the Yalkut. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Bereshit Rabbah 69:4; correct: Bereshit Rabbah 69:7)*

**[Genesis 28:17](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis_28.17)** — וַיִּירָא וַיֹּאמַר מַה נּוֹרָא הַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה אֵין זֶה כִּי אִם בֵּית אֱלֹהִים וְזֶה שַׁעַר הַשָּׁמָיִם: "He was afraid and said: How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven." The Midrash divides the verse into three clauses: built, destroyed, rebuilt. *Mafteach: found*

**[Psalms 68:36](https://www.sefaria.org/Psalms_68.36)** — נוֹרָא אֱלֹהִים מִמִּקְדָּשֶׁיךָ אֵל יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא נֹתֵן עֹז וְתַעֲצֻמוֹת לָעָם: "Awesome is God from Your sanctuaries." This is the key verse of the os: awe goes out from the Mikdash, openly when it stands and hidden when it is destroyed. *Mafteach: found*

**[Psalms 147:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Psalms_147.13)** — כִּי חִזַּק בְּרִיחֵי שְׁעָרָיִךְ בֵּרַךְ בָּנַיִךְ בְּקִרְבֵּךְ: "For He has strengthened the bars of your gates; He has blessed your children within you." The word 'gates' links this verse to 'the gate of heaven' (paragraph 3), and the 'bars' to Yaakov as the middle bar ([1.32]). *Mafteach: missing*

**[Zohar I 151b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Vayetzei_14.98)** (Vayetzei, Sitrei Torah) — סִתְרֵי תּוֹרָה: וַיַּרְא וְהִנֵּה בְאֵר בַּשָּׂדֶה... בְּאֵר, דַּרְגָּא דַּאֲדוֹן כָּל הָאָרֶץ. בַּשָּׂדֶה, חֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין קַדִּישִׁין: "'A well' is the level of 'the Lord of all the earth'; 'in the field' is the field of holy apples." The citation is exact (Vilna 151b). *Mafteach: found*

**[Genesis 29:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis_29.2)** — וַיַּרְא וְהִנֵּה בְאֵר בַּשָּׂדֶה וְהִנֵּה שָׁם שְׁלֹשָׁה עֶדְרֵי צֹאן רֹבְצִים עָלֶיהָ: "He looked, and behold, a well in the field, and three flocks of sheep lying beside it." *Mafteach: found*

**[Exodus 26:28](https://www.sefaria.org/Exodus_26.28)** — וְהַבְּרִיחַ הַתִּיכֹן בְּתוֹךְ הַקְּרָשִׁים מַבְרִחַ מִן הַקָּצֶה אֶל הַקָּצֶה: "The middle bar in the midst of the boards shall pass through from end to end." The identification with Yaakov is in **[Zohar I 148a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Vayetzei_4.29)** (Vayetzei): תָּא חֲזֵי מַה כְּתִיב בְּיַעֲקֹב שְׁלֵימָא, וְעַל יַעֲקֹב כְּתִיב וְהַבְּרִיחַ הַתִּיכוֹן בְּתוֹךְ הַקְּרָשִׁים — "of Yaakov, the complete one, it is written: the middle bar." He ties this to 'He strengthened the bars of your gates': Yaakov is the bar of the rebuilt Temple. *Mafteach: missing*
**[Genesis 2:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis_2.10)** — וְנָהָר יֹצֵא מֵעֵדֶן לְהַשְׁקוֹת אֶת הַגָּן: "A river goes out from Eden to water the garden." *Mafteach: found*

**[Zohar I 26a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Bereshit_21.247)** (Bereshit, Tikkunim section) — נָהָר דְּהֲוָה חָרֵב וְיָבֵשׁ אִתְּמַר בֵּיהּ וְנָהָר יוֹצֵא מֵעֵדֶן... וְנָהָר דָּא עַמּוּדָא דְּאֶמְצָעִיתָא, יוֹצֵא מֵעֵדֶן דָּא אִמָּא עִלָּאָה, לְהַשְׁקוֹת אֶת הַגָּן דָּא שְׁכִינְתָּא תַּתָּאָה: "The river is the central pillar; 'goes out from Eden' is the Supernal Mother; 'to water the garden' is the lower Shechinah." The passage stands at the end of 26a, as he says; it speaks of the dried river flowing again when Israel leaves exile, which fits the rebuilt Temple. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Zohar I 8a; correct: Zohar I 26a)*

**[Genesis 24:63](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis_24.63)** — וַיֵּצֵא יִצְחָק לָשׂוּחַ בַּשָּׂדֶה לִפְנוֹת עָרֶב: "Yitzchak went out to meditate in the field toward evening." **[Pesachim 88a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim_88a)** uses the same verse: וְלֹא כְּיִצְחָק שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ שָׂדֶה — Yitzchak called the Temple site 'field'. *Mafteach: found*

**[Genesis 31:42](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis_31.42)** — לוּלֵי אֱלֹהֵי אָבִי אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם וּפַחַד יִצְחָק הָיָה לִי: "Had not the God of my father, the God of Avraham and the Fear of Yitzchak, been with me." *Mafteach: missing*

**[Shulchan Arukh, Orach Chayim 1:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Shulchan_Arukh,_Orach_Chayim_1.1)** (Rema) — כְּשֶׁיָּשִׂים הָאָדָם אֶל לִבּוֹ שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ הַגָּדוֹל הקב"ה אֲשֶׁר מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ עוֹמֵד עָלָיו וְרוֹאֶה בְּמַעֲשָׂיו... מִיָּד יַגִּיעַ אֵלָיו הַיִּרְאָה: "When a person takes to heart that the great King stands over him and sees his deeds, fear comes to him at once" (the Rema cites Moreh Nevuchim 3:52). The author does not name it; for him this is Yitzchak's fear, which a person brings into his own heart, as against Yaakov's fear, which falls of itself. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels:** [Peri Tzadik, Rosh Hashanah 8](#/read/Peri_Tzadik,_Rosh_Hashanah_8) (Rav Tzadok) — the same teaching almost word for word: הַגָּדוֹל הַגִּבּוֹר וְהַנּוֹרָא correspond to the three Avos, and Yaakov is נוֹרָא, since fear falls on him from Hashem "בלא השתדלותו", while Yitzchak's fear comes from picturing that the King of kings stands over him; it also uses Pesachim 88a (Yaakov called it "house", permanence). It adds that this is why "ובכן תן פחדך" is said in the blessing Atah Kadosh, which corresponds to Yaakov. *checked*

**[Zohar II 79a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Yitro_14.246)** (Yitro) — כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמַר הָאֵל הַגָּדוֹל הַגִּבּוֹר וְהַנּוֹרָא, מַאי וְהַנּוֹרָא, דָּא יַעֲקֹב, וּכְתִיב וְיַעֲקֹב אִישׁ תָּם, כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ גְּבַר שְׁלִים: "What is 'and the awesome'? This is Yaakov" — complete in everything. The paragraph begins on 78b and ends at the top of 79a. *Mafteach: found*

**[Zohar I 26a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Bereshit_21.247)** — the same passage as above: יוֹצֵא מֵעֵדֶן דָּא אִמָּא עִלָּאָה, "'goes out from Eden' is the Supernal Mother", that is, Binah. Since the river (Yaakov) draws from Eden (Binah, root of fear), his fear comes from above and is called 'awesome'. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Zohar I 8a; correct: Zohar I 26a)*
**[Deuteronomy 10:17](https://www.sefaria.org/Deuteronomy_10.17)** — הָאֵל הַגָּדֹל הַגִּבֹּר וְהַנּוֹרָא אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִשָּׂא פָנִים: "the great, mighty and awesome God." *Mafteach: missing*
**[Zohar II 79a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Yitro_14.246)** — מַאי וְהַנּוֹרָא, דָּא יַעֲקֹב, quoted from the passage cited above ([1.57]). *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Akeidat Yitzchak, Mavo Shearim 4](https://www.sefaria.org/Akeidat_Yitzchak,_Mavo_Shearim_4)** (Machshava) — R. Yitzchak Arama links the three titles הגדול הגבור והנורא to the three Avos, with 'awesome' coming from God's watching over Yaakov ('ושמרתיך בכל אשר תלך'). He then explains the Yoma 69b passage, reading כובש את כעסו.
כִּי כָּל אֶחָד מֵהֶם הִכִּיר אֶחָד מִתְּאָרָיו אֵלֶּה ית' יוֹתֵר מִזּוּלָתוֹ

**[Yoma 69b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma_69b.14)** — אֲתָא יִרְמְיָה וְאָמַר נָכְרִים מְקַרְקְרִין בְּהֵיכָלוֹ אַיֵּה נוֹרְאוֹתָיו, לֹא אָמַר נוֹרָא; אֲתָא דָּנִיֵּאל אָמַר נָכְרִים מִשְׁתַּעְבְּדִים בְּבָנָיו אַיֵּה גְּבוּרוֹתָיו, לֹא אָמַר גִּבּוֹר; אֲתוֹ אִינְהוּ וְאָמְרוּ אַדְּרַבָּה זוֹ הִיא גְּבוּרַת גְּבוּרָתוֹ שֶׁכּוֹבֵשׁ אֶת יִצְרוֹ... וְאֵלּוּ הֵן נוֹרְאוֹתָיו שֶׁאִלְמָלֵא מוֹרָאוֹ שֶׁל הקב"ה הֵיאַךְ אֻמָּה אַחַת יְכוֹלָה לְהִתְקַיֵּם בֵּין הָאֻמּוֹת (69b:14–15). Yirmiyahu dropped 'awesome' because foreigners were shrieking in the Temple; the Men of the Great Assembly restored it: Israel's survival shows God's awe. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Agra DeKala, Lech Lecha 166](https://www.sefaria.org/Agra_DeKala,_Lech_Lecha_166)** (Chassidus) — R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov puts together Pesachim 88a (three Temples for the three Avos; the third, Yaakov's 'house', lasts forever) and Yoma 69b. Like the author, he reads 'His might' and 'His awe' as working hidden during the exile: חסד המתלבש בדין.
בַּיִת שְׁלִישִׁי שֶׁיִּבָּנֶה בִּמְהֵרָה בְּיָמֵינוּ הוּא נֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב שֶׁקְּרָאוֹ בַּיִת

**[Ein Yaakov, Yoma 7:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Ein_Yaakov,_Yoma_7.3)** — the Ein Yaakov reads: זוֹ הִיא גְּבוּרָתוֹ שֶׁכּוֹבֵשׁ אֶת כַּעֲסוֹ וְנוֹתֵן אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם לָרְשָׁעִים — "His anger" in place of the Gemara's "His inclination" (Yoma 69b:15: שֶׁכּוֹבֵשׁ אֶת יִצְרוֹ). He agrees in the end ([2.64]), because 'the might of His might' means that God holds back even His own might. *Mafteach: missing*

**[I Chronicles 29:18](https://www.sefaria.org/I_Chronicles_29.18)** — שָׁמְרָה זֹּאת לְעוֹלָם לְיֵצֶר מַחְשְׁבוֹת לְבַב עַמֶּךָ וְהָכֵן לְבָבָם אֵלֶיךָ: David's prayer after the people gave freely for the Temple. He uses it to show that יֵצֶר means desire, so 'conquers His yetzer' can be said of God. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Be'er Mayim Chaim, Leviticus 21:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Be'er_Mayim_Chaim,_Leviticus_21.4.2)** (Chassidus) — on Yoma 69b (reading מרקדין and כובש את כעסו): God's 'might of His might' is that, out of love for Israel, He holds back His mercy and His anger, like a father who forces himself to cut a thorn from his son's hand. As in the author's reading, God conquers an inner desire.
עַד שֶׁכָּבַשׁ רַחֲמָיו בִּגְבוּרָה גְּדוֹלָה מְאֹד מְאֹד

**The print reads** מְרַקְּדִין ('dance'). The Gemara and the author himself above ([2.14]) read מְקַרְקְרִין ('shriek'), but the Ein Yaakov, which he follows for כַּעְסוֹ, reads מרקדים: **[Ein Yaakov (Glick Edition), Yoma 7:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Ein_Yaakov_(Glick_Edition),_Yoma_7.3)** — אָתָא יִרְמְיָהוּ אָמַר עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים מְרַקְּדִים בְּהֵיכָלוֹ אַיֵּה נוֹרְאוֹתָיו (the Daat edition of **[Ein Yaakov, Yoma 7:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Ein_Yaakov,_Yoma_7.3)** brackets it, (מרקדים) [מְקַרְקְרִין]). So the word may come from the Ein Yaakov reading and need not be a misprint. *Mafteach: missing*

**The print reads** הַמה"ר; **read** הַמד"ר (the Midrash Rabbah), since the next line says וְכֵן הֻקְשָׁה לְהַמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה. The reference is to **[Bereshit Rabbah 69:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah_69.7)**: בָּנוּי וְחָרֵב וּבָנוּי. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Bereshit Rabbah 69:4; correct: Bereshit Rabbah 69:7)*

**[Zohar I 151a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Vayetzei_12.83)** (Vayetzei) — יִהְיֶה בֵּית אֱלֹהִים לְעָלְמִין. בֵּית אֱלֹהִים, בֵּית יְיָ מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ, כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמַר... בֵּית יְיָ נֵלֵךְ, אֶלָּא אֲתַר דְּבֵי דִּינָא אִיהוּ: "'House of Elohim' — it should have said 'house of Hashem'... rather, it is a place of judgment." The Zohar answers with judgment; the author answers that 'Elohim' is the Name that remains in the destroyed Temple, where the awe is hidden. *Mafteach: found*

**[Genesis 28:22](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis_28.22)** — וְהָאֶבֶן הַזֹּאת אֲשֶׁר שַׂמְתִּי מַצֵּבָה יִהְיֶה בֵּית אֱלֹהִים: "This stone, which I have set up as a pillar, shall be the house of God." *Mafteach: missing*

**[Psalms 122:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Psalms_122.1)** — שִׁיר הַמַּעֲלוֹת לְדָוִד שָׂמַחְתִּי בְּאֹמְרִים לִי בֵּית יְהוָה נֵלֵךְ: "I rejoiced when they said to me: Let us go to the house of Hashem." *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Be'er Mayim Chaim, Genesis 28:17](https://www.sefaria.org/Be'er_Mayim_Chaim,_Genesis_28.17.1)** (Chassidus) — R. Chaim of Czernowitz reads the same Midrash (built, destroyed, built) on 'אין זה כי אם בית אלהים': Elohim is Malchut, the Shechinah that never left the Western Wall, so even the destroyed Temple remains 'house of Elohim' and is awesome. This is very close to the author's point that the Name Elohim remains in the destruction.
וְזֶה אוֹמְרָם "אֵין זֶה" הֲרֵי חָרֵב, כְּלוֹמַר בְּחֻרְבָּנוֹ... וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן כָּל כָּךְ גָּדְלָה הַקְּדֻשָּׁה שֶׁבָּהּ

**[Matnot Kehunah on Bereshit Rabbah 69:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Matnot_Kehunah_on_Bereshit_Rabbah_69.7.5)** — ה"ג בֵּית אֱלֹהִים וְגוֹ' בָּנוּי וּמְשׁוּכְלָל, וְדַיֵּיק מִסֵּיפֵיהּ דִּקְרָא דִּכְתִיב וְזֶה שַׁעַר הַשָּׁמַיִם וּכְתִיב הָתָם כִּי חִזַּק בְּרִיחֵי שְׁעָרָיִךְ, וְהָכִי מוּכָח בְּיַלְקוּט בְּהֶדְיָא: the proof-verse 'bars of your gates' must belong to the clause 'gate of heaven'. The Sefaria/Vilna text of the Midrash still carries the reading the author rejects ('כי אם בית אלהים — בנוי ומשכלל'). *Mafteach: missing*

**[Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 120:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Yalkut_Shimoni_on_Torah_120.4)** — אֵין זֶה, הֲרֵי חָרֵב... וְזֶה שַׁעַר הַשָּׁמַיִם, הֲרֵי בָּנוּי וּמְשֻׁכְלָל לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא, כְּמָה דְּאַתְּ אָמַר כִּי חִזַּק בְּרִיחֵי שְׁעָרָיִךְ. The Yalkut has the reading he defends, word for word. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Rashi on Exodus 15:17](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Exodus_15.17.2)** (Beshalach) — מָכוֹן לְשִׁבְתְּךָ: מִקְדָּשׁ שֶׁל מַטָּה מְכֻוָּן כְּנֶגֶד כִּסֵּא שֶׁל מַעְלָה. Rashi gives the Mekhilta as his source and speaks of the Throne above. The Temple-above-against-Temple-below wording is in the Midrash Rabbah itself, **[Bereshit Rabbah 69:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah_69.7)**: אֵין בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁל מַעְלָן גָּבוֹהַּ מִבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁל מַטָּן אֶלָּא שְׁמוֹנָה עָשָׂר מִיל, מַה טַּעַם וְזֶה שַׁעַר הַשָּׁמַיִם — on the very clause he is explaining. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Exodus 15:14; correct: Rashi on Exodus 15:17)*

**[Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 30a](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Rosh_Hashanah_30a.23.1)** — דְּאֵין בִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ לֹא בְּיוֹם טוֹב וְלֹא בַּלַּיְלָה, הָנֵי מִילֵּי בִּנְיַן בִּידֵי אָדָם, אֲבָל בִּנְיַן הֶעָתִיד לָבֹא בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם הוּא: "the future building is by the hands of Heaven." The comment stands at the end of 30a, as he says. *Mafteach: found*

**[Pesachim 88a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim_88a)** — לֹא כְּאַבְרָהָם שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ הַר... וְלֹא כְּיִצְחָק שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ שָׂדֶה... אֶלָּא כְּיַעֲקֹב שֶׁקְּרָאוֹ בַּיִת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וַיִּקְרָא אֶת שֵׁם הַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא בֵּית אֵל: Yaakov called it 'house'. A house is a fixed dwelling, so for him the word means permanent holiness, which stays even in the destruction. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Pesachim 86a; correct: Pesachim 88a)*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Avodat Yisrael, Sefer Bereshit, Vayetzei 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodat_Yisrael,_Sefer_Bereshit,_Vayetzei_2)** (Chassidus) — the Kozhnitzer Maggid joins Pesachim 88a ('Yaakov called it house') to the third Temple that will never be destroyed, and reads 'he was afraid... this is none other than the house of God' as Yaakov's fear on seeing the long last exile. This is the same link of 'house' to permanence.
הַבַּיִת שֶׁיִּבָּנֶה ב"ב נֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב שְׁלִימוּ דַּאֲבָהָן וּמִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵמָה וְלֹא יִהְיֶה לוֹ הֶרֶס

**[Psalms 27:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Psalms_27.4)** — אַחַת שָׁאַלְתִּי מֵאֵת יְהוָה אוֹתָהּ אֲבַקֵּשׁ שִׁבְתִּי בְּבֵית יְהוָה כָּל יְמֵי חַיַּי לַחֲזוֹת בְּנֹעַם יְהוָה וּלְבַקֵּר בְּהֵיכָלוֹ. He applies it to Shabbat, when Israel can feel the holiness of the Mikdash. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels:** [Peri Tzadik, Tetzaveh 12](#/read/Peri_Tzadik,_Tetzaveh_12) (Rav Tzadok) — also about Shabbat: "תיכף בכניסת השבת נופל עליו הפחד והיראה", with the Shabbat-night meal set against Yitzchak and fear that comes "כשרואה ממ"ה הקב"ה עומד עליו" (the Rema wording of [1.51]). It adds the Kohen's lamps and incense: on Shabbat every Jew is like a Kohen in the Mikdash. *checked*

**[Zohar I 153a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Vayetzei_15.120)** (Vayetzei) — לְהַהוּא אֲתַר דְּיַעֲקֹב דְּאִיהוּ רְתִיכָא עִלָּאָה, וְאַמְשִׁיךְ בִּרְכָאן לְהַהוּא אֲתַר מִמַּבּוּעָא דְּכָל מַבּוּעִין: charity rises 'to the place of Yaakov, the supernal chariot, and he draws blessings to that place from the spring of all springs'. He reads the spring as Eden. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Mikdash Melekh on Zohar 1:153a](https://www.sefaria.org/Mikdash_Melekh_on_Zohar_1.153a.3)** (Kabbalah) — R. Shalom Buzaglo, on the same Zohar line, explains that Zeir Anpin (Yaakov's place) draws blessing from Imma. This is what the author means by 'from Eden', that is, Binah.
וְאַמְשִׁיךְ בִּרְכָאן לְהַהוּא אֲתַר שֶׁהוּא זְעִיר מִמַּבּוּעָא דְּכָל מַבּוּעִין שֶׁהִיא אִימָּא

**[Zohar I 152b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Vayetzei_14.96)** (Vayetzei) — תָּא חֲזֵי הַאי בְּאֵר שֶׁבַע זִמְנִין כְּתִיב בְּפַרְשְׁתָּא דָא, בְּגִין דְּאִיהוּ רֶמֶז לְשֶׁבַע... הָא שִׁבְעָה וּבְוַדַּאי דְּהָכִי הוּא: 'well' appears seven times in this parashah, an allusion to the seven (Be'er Sheva). He gives no page; it is 152b. *Mafteach: missing*
**[Exodus 2:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Exodus_2.15)** — וַיִּבְרַח מֹשֶׁה מִפְּנֵי פַרְעֹה וַיֵּשֶׁב בְּאֶרֶץ מִדְיָן וַיֵּשֶׁב עַל הַבְּאֵר. *Mafteach: found*

**[Tikkunei Zohar 29a](https://www.sefaria.org/Tikkunei_Zohar_29a.7)** — וְיַעֲקֹב וַדַּאי אִיהוּ דְּיוֹקְנָא דְּעַמּוּדָא דְּאֶמְצָעִיתָא מִסִּטְרָא דִּלְבַר, וְהָא מֹשֶׁה תַּמָּן הֲוָה אֶלָּא מִסִּטְרָא דִּלְגָאו הֲוָה, דָּא מִגּוּפָא וְדָא מִנִּשְׁמָתָא. The quotation is exact; he gives it as Tikkun 13 (Sefaria 29a:7). *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** [Peri Tzadik, Vayetzei 8](#/read/Peri_Tzadik,_Vayetzei_8) (Rav Tzadok) — brings together the same two sources, Zohar I 152b (seven wells; Moshe "מאריה דביתא ואסתלק לעילא... על הבאר") and Tikkun 13 ("דא מגופא ודא מנשמתא"). It adds that Yaakov, as the body, refined the bodies of Israel in the seven years until Yosef was born, while Moshe brought down the Torah, the root of the souls. *checked*

**[Zohar I 152b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Vayetzei_14.97)** (Vayetzei) — בְּמֹשֶׁה לָא כְּתִיב אֶלָּא זִמְנָא חֲדָא... בְּגִין דְּמֹשֶׁה כַּד עָאל אִתְפְּרַשׁ מִכֹּל וָכֹל מִבֵּיתָא דִּלְתַתָּא, וְיַעֲקֹב לָא אִתְפְּרַשׁ כְּלָל... וּבְגִין כָּךְ מֹשֶׁה מָארֵיהּ דְּבֵיתָא הֲוָה... בְּמֹשֶׁה כְּתִיב וַיֵּשֶׁב עַל הַבְּאֵר, בְּיַעֲקֹב וַיַּרְא וְהִנֵּה בְאֵר. This is the passage behind his contrast: Moshe, master of the house, 'sat by the well' (once); Yaakov 'saw the well' (seven times). He does not name it; it comes right after the seven-wells passage. *Mafteach: missing*
**[Deuteronomy 33:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Deuteronomy_33.1)** — וְזֹאת הַבְּרָכָה אֲשֶׁר בֵּרַךְ מֹשֶׁה אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לִפְנֵי מוֹתוֹ. *Mafteach: found*

**[Zohar II 22b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Vaera_1.12)** (Vaera) — מֹשֶׁה אִלְמָלֵא דַּהֲוָה מָארֵיהּ דְּבֵיתָא אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים אִתְעֲנַשׁ עַל מַה דְּאָמַר: "Had Moshe not been master of the house, man of God, he would have been punished." The Zohar uses this phrase for Moshe in several places (also Zohar I 152b, in the note above). *Mafteach: found*

**[Midrash Tanchuma, V'Zot HaBerachah 2:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tanchuma,_V'Zot_HaBerachah_2.1)** — מֹשֶׁה אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים... אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אִלְמָלֵא מִקְרָא כָּתוּב אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְאָמְרוֹ, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָדָם גּוֹזֵר עַל אִשְׁתּוֹ וְעוֹשָׂה, כָּךְ הקב"ה גָּזַר עַל מֹשֶׁה וְעָשָׂה לוֹ. The printed text reverses the roles out of reverence (see the Sefaria translator's note there); the sense, as the author reads it, is that Moshe decreed and God fulfilled. The exact words 'וְהָיָה מֹשֶׁה גּוֹזֵר וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְקַיֵּם' appear in **[Midrash Tanchuma, Vaera 3:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tanchuma,_Vaera_3.2)**. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Tanchuma 3 (no parasha given); correct: Tanchuma, V'Zot HaBerachah 2)*
